statement.p: Let T({\bf x})=A{\bf x} for the matrix A and
Select true or false for each statement.

The vector \bf{c} is in the range of T.
???
True
False

The vector \bf{b} is in the kernel of T.
???
True
False

static.solution:
A{\bf b}=\left[\begin{array}{ccc} 5 \amp -1 \amp 13\cr -2 \amp 0 \amp -6\cr 7 \amp -5 \amp 11 \end{array}\right] \left[\begin{array}{c}-3\\-2\\1\\\end{array}\right]= \left[\begin{array}{c}0\\0\\0\\\end{array}\right] ={\bf 0}, so {\bf b}\in \ker(T).
Row-reduce to determine a solution of A{\bf x}={\bf c}.
\left[\begin{array}{cccc} 5 \amp -1 \amp 13 \amp -1\cr -2 \amp 0 \amp -6 \amp 0\cr 7 \amp -5 \amp 11 \amp -5 \end{array}\right] \sim \left[\begin{array}{cccc} 1 \amp 0 \amp 3 \amp 0\cr 0 \amp 1 \amp 2 \amp 1\cr 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \end{array}\right].
or simply notice that \bf{c} is the second column of \bf{A}. Row reduction shows that the equation \bf{A}\bf{x}=\bf{c} has infinitely many solutions:
\bf{x} = \left[\begin{array}{c}0\\1\\0\\\end{array}\right] + t \left[\begin{array}{c}-3\\-2\\1\\\end{array}\right] for arbitrary t \in \mathbb{R},
and both approaches lead to the conclusion that
A \left[\begin{array}{c}0\\1\\0\\\end{array}\right] = {\bf c}.
Thus {\bf c}\in range(T).
